svg.text: Row-level security — the database refuses to show rows that aren't yours
Without RLS — safety depends on the developer
SELECT * FROM booking WHERE id = 4471;
Developer forgot AND tenant_id = … — it happens
Returns another tenant's booking. Breach.
With RLS — safety is a property of the data
SELECT * FROM booking WHERE id = 4471;
Exactly the same buggy query
Returns 0 rows. The policy rewrote it.
What you write once, at setup
ALTER TABLE booking ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY t_isolation ON booking USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id')::uuid);
What happens per request
SET LOCAL app.tenant_id = 'nyati-uuid';
Set by the interceptor, inside the transaction,
from the verified token — never from user input.
The two traps
1. Table owners and SUPERUSER bypass RLS by default —
your app must connect as a non-owner role.
2. Use SET LOCAL, or a pooled connection leaks the value.
